world.org_type: a regional airline flying 30 twin turboprops on short coastal routes, with a component shop at its Bodø base

driver: Each unit's forward demand is the sum of event streams that follow different exposures, and the record's exposures moved together, so every in-sample check passes on the conventional one while the forward plan decouples them; part of the stream is repeated swaps driven by a fault in the host rather than the item, so the items flagged by their own counts are mostly the host's victims or chance and regress; a fix converts the population item by item at each item's own visit; every line's turnaround runs through one shared queue that lengthens nonlinearly as the forward load rises; and demand clusters in shared shocks, so the stock each line needs is set by the clustered, queue-lengthened pipeline, never by its average.
driver_concrete: Each rotable's 2027 spares need is its unscheduled removals under the 2027 programme (the landing- and start-driven parts on landings, which the Helgeland short sectors raise 19 per cent while flight hours fall 13 per cent, not on flight hours as the reliability report projects), returned through the Bodø shop's queue, which the 2027 load stretches to about 29 days in the summer holiday weeks against 13 across 2026, with the watch list read for the serials whose own record repeats
stump: A careful but hurried analyst projects each part on its twelve-month removals per flight hour, sizes spares by Palm's formula on the 2026 average turnaround and withdraws the watch-list serials with confirmed failures: it holds 5 starter-generators and cuts the brakes to 4 where the plan needs 9 and 9, cuts the avionics right, and withdraws 4 serials (one an aircraft's victim) where 8 repeat on their own record
deep_chain: (1) each part's confirmed failures fitted on landings, flight hours and calendar days across the bases' sector lengths, the landing-driven ones carried on the 2027 programme's landings; (2) the propeller control's SB 61-0042 conversion rebuilt from each serial's spells and the repairers' returns; (3) the Bodø shop replayed on its own roster and work orders, calibrated to its 2024 to 2026 turnarounds, at 2027's load through the staggered summer holidays; (4) the watch list read serial by serial, the runs of serviceable removals one aircraft position drove set aside, each serial's own rate in a two-group model; (5) each pool replayed through 2027 for the 95 per cent fill rate
judgment: an exposure basis the record's collinear hours and landings hide in aggregate and the bases' sector lengths separate; a removal count that measures the aircraft's fault and chance before the serial; a shared queue that nets every in-house line against the others' load in the holiday weeks
one_fact_test: the strongest sentence (the starter-generators, brakes and bleed valves wear by landings and starts, which the 2027 programme raises while hours fall) rescues R2 and none of the watch list, the bulletin, the shop's turnaround, the ranges or the spares lines, which still carry the watch list's counts, the 2026 rate, the average turnaround and Poisson demand: 1 of 9

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a count of alerts each unit raises when its departure from an estimate built from its nearest other units passes a limit set from that departure's past spread; when some units leave, the remaining units' estimates come from farther units and their departures spread wider while their limits stay at the spread measured with the old neighbours, so the alerts rise even as the units fall.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is a count of alerts a less sensitive limit will raise, read from a record the current limit produced: every fault the current limit caught was repaired within days, so the record holds those faults cut short below the higher limit they would otherwise have reached, and the count is the record re-run on the units and estimate sources the next period will have plus one alert for every caught fault the re-run never alerted before its repair.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is each node's share of the units that passed through it unrecorded, when which node an unrecorded unit passed is itself unrecorded: the plan of record assigns every unit a node, but on the nights one node overflowed part of its flow went through a second node and was handled there by hand, so that night's unrecorded units belong partly to each and only the batch a unit was unloaded in at its destination, whose recorded members all passed one node, says which; charged by the plan the overflowing node carries the second node's misses, and charged by the nights' excess over its usual rate the overflowing node sheds the misses its own overload caused.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what handing a set of members of shared sequences to an outside provider saves, the time the sequences would no longer take: a member the sequence passes through on its way to others saves only its own stops beyond the direct run between its neighbours, and on a branch the near member saves the branch only when the members beyond it go too, so pricing each member at the time its own stops and the run into them take credits passed-through members with travel the sequences still make and, member by member, keeps the near member of a branch.

lineage.driver: A forward workload is forecast through a per-unit rate that rises once more workers share a fixed space, a rise the coarse record hides because the busy periods carry lighter units, so a proportional scaling its own back-test confirms plans the busy periods short; the forward volume comes from a forecaster whose overstatement grows with the growth it plans and whose period profile is keyed to a calendar grid that a long year moves a whole step against the events driving demand, and a new stream's per-unit work is measured on a pilot whose units were drawn from its lightest class, so which periods need a second shift and how many extra hours to book come out only when every correction is carried together.
lineage.driver_concrete: Saarnela's 2027 peak plan forecasts each small-parts zone's paid picker hours from Kotikaari Oy's year-ahead weekly forecast, which overstates by a share that grows with the growth it plans and copies 2025's week numbers into a calendar shifted a week by 2026's 53 ISO weeks (Black Friday falls in week 47 of 2027), through a time per line by handling class and units with an aisle-congestion term that the peak's lighter lines hide in the weekly record, and with Huippu Sport's lines at its full peak assortment (footwear boxes, multi-unit lines) where the September pilot stocked only polybag apparel; the day shift's capacity at each zone's limit of pickers on the floor decides the evening-shift weeks and the remainder sets the agency booking; on the cut pack the golden opens the evening shift in weeks 47 to 50 in both zones (week 46 at 0.84 and 0.87 of the day shifts' capacity, weeks 47 to 50 at 1.17 to 1.30), the draft's route in week 48 only.
lineage.stump: The careful pass measures the pooled overstatement (right) and applies it to every week of the client's 2027 forecast, keeping the forecast's week-numbered profile (Black Friday a week late) and pricing its planned growth at the pooled rate; it fits time per line on the handling-class mix at the weekly or shift grain, where the peak's lighter lines hide the aisle congestion, so the 2025 peak's rate carries to 2027's denser floor and the draft's back-test confirms it; and it reads Huippu Sport's time per line off the pilot, whose polybag assortment picks quicker than Kotikaari's lines: it books too few agency hours in the busiest weeks and opens the evening shift in the wrong weeks.
